docs.title: 2. Implementing the AirDbAdapter
docs.text:
package io.airdb.storage.sqldelight

import io.airdb.adapter.AirDbAdapter
import io.airdb.adapter.ChangeRecord
import io.airdb.adapter.HlcComparator
import io.airdb.adapter.MutationType

class SqlDelightAirDbAdapter(
    private val db: Database
) : AirDbAdapter {

    private val queries = db.airDbChangelogQueries

    override suspend fun getChangesSince(sinceHlcTimestamp: String?, limit: Int): List<ChangeRecord> {
        val rows = if (sinceHlcTimestamp == null) {
            queries.getEarliestChanges(limit.toLong()).executeAsList()
        } else {
            queries.getChangesAfter(sinceHlcTimestamp, limit.toLong()).executeAsList()
        }

        return rows.map { row ->
            ChangeRecord(
                id = row.id,
                collection = row.collection,
                type = MutationType.fromCode(row.mutation_type.toInt()),
                payload = row.payload,
                hlcTimestamp = row.hlc_timestamp,
                authorPublicKey = row.author_public_key,
                signature = row.signature
            )
        }
    }

    override suspend fun applyChanges(changes: List<ChangeRecord>) {
        db.transaction {
            for (change in changes) {
                // Apply LWW and insert into changelog
                queries.upsertChange(
                    collection = change.collection,
                    id = change.id,
                    mutationType = change.type.code.toLong(),
                    payload = change.payload,
                    hlcTimestamp = change.hlcTimestamp,
                    authorPublicKey = change.authorPublicKey,
                    signature = change.signature,
                    createdAt = System.currentTimeMillis()
                )
            }
        }
    }

    override suspend fun getLatestHlc(): String? {
        return queries.getLatestHlc().executeAsOneOrNull()?.MAX
    }
}

docs.title: Built-in SQLite Storage Engine
docs.text:
AirDB includes an optimized, production-grade SQLite persistence engine out of the box: - On Android and Kotlin JVM: SqliteDbAdapter in :airdb-adapter-sqlite. - On Apple Platforms (iOS/macOS): SqliteDbAdapter in AirDbKit (backed by native libsqlite3).

It requires zero manual SQL queries, configures high-performance Write-Ahead Logging (WAL) automatically, and provides crash resilience with atomic batch transactions.

docs.title: 1. Quick Initialization
2. Under the Hood: Tables & Performance Primitives
docs.text: When initialized, the SQLite adapter automatically executes the following performance optimizations and schema setup:

docs.title: Pragmas
docs.text:
• PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL;: Enables Write-Ahead Logging. Readers never block writers, and writers never block readers.
  • PRAGMA synchronous = NORMAL;: Reduces disk sync overhead while maintaining full durability against application crashes.
  • PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON;: Enforces relational integrity.

docs.title: Tables
docs.text:
1. airdb_entities: Stores the latest known state of each entity: 

    CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS airdb_entities (
    collection TEXT NOT NULL,
    id TEXT NOT NULL,
    type INTEGER NOT NULL,
    payload BLOB NOT NULL,
    hlc_timestamp TEXT NOT NULL,
    updated_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (collection, id)
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_entities_hlc ON airdb_entities (hlc_timestamp);

  2. airdb_changelog: An append-only sequence tracking every applied mutation: 

    CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS airdb_changelog (
    seq INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    collection TEXT NOT NULL,
    id TEXT NOT NULL,
    type INTEGER NOT NULL,
    payload BLOB NOT NULL,
    hlc_timestamp TEXT NOT NULL,
    created_at INTEGER NOT NULL
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_changelog_hlc ON airdb_changelog (hlc_timestamp);

docs.title: 3. Atomic Transactions & Conflict Resolution
docs.text: When a batch of remote mutations arrives from a peer: 1. The adapter starts an immediate transaction (BEGIN IMMEDIATE). 2. For each change record, it compares the incoming HLC timestamp against the stored entity's timestamp using HlcComparator. 3. If the incoming change is newer, the live table airdb_entities is updated and an entry is appended to airdb_changelog. 4. If an error occurs or the process is killed midway, SQLite cleanly rolls back the entire batch, preserving database consistency.

docs.title: Testing Without Hardware (Sans-I/O Simulation)
docs.text:
Testing distributed Bluetooth applications on physical hardware is notoriously slow. Pairing phones, managing battery levels, walking across rooms to test range, and waiting for radio timeouts makes automated continuous integration (CI) painful.

AirDB embraces a Sans-I/O architecture that completely separates networking protocols and causality state machines from physical hardware radios.

docs.title: 1. What is Sans-I/O?
docs.text:
In a traditional library, state logic is tightly coupled to socket delegates or Android Bluetooth callbacks.

In AirDB: - The core engine (AirDbEngine), wire codecs (BinaryCodec), and causality trackers (HybridLogicalClock, VectorClock) are pure standard Kotlin / Swift. They take bytes or events in, perform state transformations, and emit outgoing packets. - Bluetooth hardware code lives exclusively inside transport drivers (AndroidBleTransport and CoreBluetoothTransport). - Both drivers implement the universal AirDbTransport interface.

Because of this seam, we can swap out the physical Bluetooth radio with SimulatedTransport!

docs.title: 2. Running In-Memory Multi-Node Tests
docs.text:
You can spin up an entire simulated Bluetooth mesh network in a single unit test:

import io.airdb.adapter.MemoryDbAdapter
import io.airdb.adapter.MutationType
import io.airdb.core.engine.AirDbEngine
import io.airdb.transport.sim.SimulatedNetwork
import io.airdb.transport.sim.SimulatedTransport
import kotlinx.coroutines.runBlocking
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertEquals
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test

class MultiNodeSyncTest {

    @Test
    fun testTwoNodeConvergence() = runBlocking {
        // 1. Create a simulated virtual radio space
        val network = SimulatedNetwork()

        // 2. Initialize Node A (Outpost Alpha)
        val dbA = MemoryDbAdapter()
        val transportA = SimulatedTransport("node-A", network)
        val engineA = AirDbEngine("node-A", dbA, transportA)

        // 3. Initialize Node B (Outpost Beta)
        val dbB = MemoryDbAdapter()
        val transportB = SimulatedTransport("node-B", network)
        val engineB = AirDbEngine("node-B", dbB, transportB)

        // 4. Save offline records on Node A
        engineA.saveRecord("patients", "p-01", MutationType.INSERT, "Alice".toByteArray())

        // 5. Connect nodes virtually and start engines
        engineA.start()
        engineB.start()

        // Give the virtual radio 100 milliseconds to complete the 4-phase sync
        kotlinx.coroutines.delay(100)

        // 6. Assert that Node B received and applied the record!
        val recordsOnB = dbB.getAllRecords("patients")
        assertEquals(1, recordsOnB.size)
        assertEquals("Alice", String(recordsOnB["p-01"]!!.payload))
    }
}

This test runs in less than 200 milliseconds on your laptop or inside GitHub Actions CI, with zero physical radios, zero flakiness, and 100% deterministic results.

docs.title: 3. Running the Interactive Simulation Demo
docs.text:
AirDB includes a ready-to-run CLI demonstration simulating two disaster response outposts exchanging medical triage and relief supplies:

cd airdb
./gradlew :airdb-samples:airdb-sim-demo:run

You can view the full source code for the demonstration in airdb-samples/airdb-sim-demo/src/main/kotlin/io/airdb/demo/DisasterReliefDemo.kt.

docs.title: API Contracts Reference
docs.text: This reference summarizes the core public interfaces, classes, and types across both Kotlin and Swift implementations.

docs.title: 1. AirDbEngine
docs.text:
The central coordinator managing state synchronization, clock ratcheting, and peer communication.

KotlinSwift 
package io.airdb.core.engine

class AirDbEngine(
    val nodeName: String,
    val adapter: AirDbAdapter,
    val transport: AirDbTransport,
    val clusterKey: ByteArray? = null,

) : TransportListener {

        collection: String,

        type: MutationType,
        payload: ByteArray
    ): ChangeRecord

    fun addSyncListener(listener: (peerId: String, changeCount: Int) -> Unit)
}

import AirDbKit

    public init(
        nodeName: String,

        transport: any AirDbTransport,

docs.title: 2. AirDbAdapter & ChangeRecord
docs.text:
The persistence seam decoupling database engines from synchronization logic.

package io.airdb.adapter

interface AirDbAdapter {
    suspend fun getChangesSince(sinceHlcTimestamp: String?, limit: Int = 100): List<ChangeRecord>
    suspend fun applyChanges(changes: List<ChangeRecord>)

    val id: String,

)

docs.title: 3. AirDbTransport & TransportEvent
docs.text:
The radio abstraction decoupling Bluetooth drivers and simulators from the engine.

KotlinSwift 
package io.airdb.transport

interface AirDbTransport {
    fun start()
    fun stop()
    fun send(packet: AirDbPacket, targetPeerId: String? = null)
    fun setListener(listener: TransportListener)
}

sealed class TransportEvent {
    data class LinkConnected(val peerId: String, val linkId: String) : TransportEvent()
    data class LinkDisconnected(val peerId: String, val linkId: String) : TransportEvent()
    data class PacketReceived(val packet: AirDbPacket, val peerId: String) : TransportEvent()

    func start() async
    func stop() async

}

public enum TransportEvent: Sendable {
    case linkConnected(peerId: String, linkId: String)
    case linkDisconnected(peerId: String, linkId: String)
    case packetReceived(packet: AirDbPacket, peerId: String)
}

docs.title: Wire Protocol Specification Reference
docs.text: This document serves as the formal specification for AirDB binary packet serialization over Bluetooth Low Energy.

docs.title: 1. Encoding Standard
docs.text:
• Endianness: All multi-byte numeric values (Short, Int, Long) are encoded in Network Byte Order (Big-Endian).
  • String Encodings: All string identifiers (node IDs, collection names, entity keys, HLC timestamps) are encoded as raw UTF-8 bytes.

docs.title: 2. Fixed Packet Header (AirDbPacket)
docs.text:
Every AirDB packet transmitted over the wire begins with a fixed header (23 bytes without recipient, or 31 bytes if a recipient ID is present):

Fixed Header Layout:
+-------------------+------------+-----------+------------+
| Field Name        | Size       | Type      | Offset (B) |
+-------------------+------------+-----------+------------+
| Magic Bytes       | 2 bytes    | ASCII     | 0 - 1      | Fixed 0x41 0x44 ("AD")
| Protocol Version  | 1 byte     | UInt8     | 2          | Current: 0x01
| Packet Type Code  | 1 byte     | UInt8     | 3          | See Section 3
| Bitmask Flags     | 1 byte     | Bitmask   | 4          | See Section 4
| Creation Time     | 8 bytes    | Int64 BE  | 5 - 12     | Epoch milliseconds
| Payload Length    | 2 bytes    | UInt16 BE | 13 - 14    | Byte length of payload
| Sender Node ID    | 8 bytes    | Int64 BE  | 15 - 22    | 64-bit sender hash
| [Recipient ID]*   | 8 bytes    | Int64 BE  | 23 - 30    | Present if FLAG_HAS_RECIPIENT
+-------------------+------------+-----------+------------+
| Variable Trailing Payload (0 to 65,535 bytes)           |
+---------------------------------------------------------+

docs.title: 3. Packet Type Codes
docs.text: Code Name Description 0x01 HANDSHAKE Initiates peer link session; payload contains sender node name UTF-8. 0x02 HANDSHAKE_ACK Confirms link session; payload contains responder node name UTF-8. 0x03 RECONCILE_REQ Transmits local Vector Clock to request missing changes. 0x04 RECONCILE_RESP Transmits peer Vector Clock in response. 0x05 DELTA_BATCH Carries serialized database mutations missing on the remote peer. 0x06 DELTA_ACK Confirms that a delta batch was verified and applied to local storage. 0x0F FRAGMENT Encapsulates a chunk of an oversized packet exceeding link MTU.

docs.title: 4. Bitmask Flags
docs.text: Bit Position Value Constant Name Description Bit 0 0x01 FLAG_COMPRESSED Payload is compressed with zlib Deflate. Bit 1 0x02 FLAG_HAS_RECIPIENT Packet header contains 8-byte recipient ID (31-byte total header). Bit 2 0x04 FLAG_ENCRYPTED Payload is encrypted with ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD.

docs.title: Authenticated Additional Data (AAD)
docs.text: The entire packet header (23 bytes or 31 bytes) is passed directly as \(AAD\) to the cipher. Any tampering with header fields invalidates the Poly1305 tag and causes the packet to be discarded immediately.

docs.title: 6. Fragment Envelope (FRAGMENT = 0x0F)
docs.text:
When a packet exceeds MTU bounds, it is split into slices wrapped in a 13-byte fragment envelope:

+--------------------+------------------+------------------+--------------------+------------+
| Fragment ID (8B)   | Index (2B BE)    | Total (2B BE)    | Original Type (1B) | Chunk Data |
+--------------------+------------------+------------------+--------------------+------------+
  • Fragment ID (8 bytes): Random Long identifying all chunks of a single packet.
  • Index (2 bytes): 0-based chunk index.
  • Total (2 bytes): Total chunks in this assembly.
  • Original Type (1 byte): Packet type code of the unfragmented message.
  • AssemblyBuffer TTL: Receivers purge incomplete assemblies after 30 seconds.

docs.title: Mutation Type Byte:
docs.text:
• Bits 0–6:
  • 0x00: INSERT
  • 0x01: UPDATE
  • 0x02: DELETE
  • Bit 7 (0x80): FLAG_RECORD_SIGNED (asserted if author public key and signature follow payload bytes).
